2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the petitioner Nos. 1-2, 12-14 and the predecessor of the petitioner Nos.3-11 as plaintiffs instituted Civil Suit No. 118 of 1988 subsequently (re-numbered as Civil Suit No. 132 of 1994) before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla for declaration of Title alleging that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No.11 corresponding to Hal Khatian No. 40 of Mouja Porkara under Police Station Chowddagram originally belonged to Dula Mia and his brother namely-Sekandar Ali with equal 8 annas share, for arrears of rent superior landlord obtained decree in rent suit without serving any notice and one Abdul Hakim shown to be auction purchaser. Abdul Hakim never obtained possession in pursuance of the decree passed in the rent suit. Dula Mia and his brother remained in possession of the suit property as before. Subsequently, Dula Mia filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for setting aside the auction and Abdul Hakim filed Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 against Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar Ali and their mother for possession of the auction purchased land. Both the suits were disposed of in accordance with solenama and in terms of solenama 45 decimals of land were given settlement in favour of Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia from RS Plot No.415. Abdul Hakim Majumder settled 96 decimals of land by way of unregistered patta dated 15-10-1948 in favour of Dula Mia at Selami of Taka 145 but in the patta wrongly RS Plot No.415 written and possession was given on RS Plot No.1246 in favour of Dula Mia. Dula Mia remained in possession of the property under plot No.1246 entirely and 8 annas share of land under plot No.3 and paid rents for schedule Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6 and for half share of RS Plot No.415 of schedule No. 3. 

 3. During Revisional settlement SA Khatian No.40 was prepared in the name of Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar. Dula Mia died leaving the plaintiffs as heirs and the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. Sekandar Ali, brother of Dula Mia remained in possession of schedule No. 3 and transferred the property under schedule Nos.7-9 in favour of the plaintiffs by registered deed dated 2-1-1976. The defendants have no manner right, title and interest in the suit land. The defendants claimed title on the suit land on 15-7-1988, hence the suit. Subsequently, the plaintiffs brought an amendment of the plaint on 14-6-1995 and claimed title on adverse possession. 

 4. The defendant Nos.1-3, 6, 11, 16, 20 and 24 entered appearance in the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit property under CS Khatian No.11 was auction sold and Abdul Hakim Majumder auction purchased the Jote under CS Khatian No.11 and got possession of the same excepting 7 decimals of land under plot No.360 and 13 decimals of land under Plot No. 361 and 4 decimals of land under Plot No. 365 total 24 decimals of land and for possession of which Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 in the Court of 3rd Munsif, Comilla against the predecessor of the plaintiffs Dula Mia and Sekandar Ali and others. The suit was disposed of in terms of Solenama with the defendant Nos.1-3, 15-18 of that suit. According to the terms of Solenama 45 decimals of land including 24 decimals of land was given settlement in favour of Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia for 5 years and after expiry of the said period since Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar Ali did not execute any Kabuliyat in favour of Abdul Hakim Majumder he filed Other Suit No. 92 of 1942 against them for recovery of possession of that land. In execution of that suit he got possession over the same on 7-2-1943. 

 11. He further submits that the plaintiffs by adducing oral evidence proved plaint case that they are possessing the suit land and the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs were recorded in CS and SA Khatians in consideration of their physical possession in the suit land and the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land by paying rent and taxes to the authority since they are predecessors but the Courts below without proper perusal of the exhibits on record improperly found that the CS record was not prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff which is a wrong findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below, thus, committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 21. On perusal of the record it appears that the predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners namely Dula Mia and his brother namely Sekander Ali were the original owners of the suit land evidencing from the CS Khatian (Exhibit-1(Ka)) and RS Khatian (Exhbit-1). The predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for settlement. The predecessor of the Defendants-Opposite Parties No. 1-3 instituted Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 for recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed on 11-10-1939 on Solenama (Exhibit-2) according to Solenama, 0.45 acre were settled to Dula Mia and Sekender Ali. As per terms of Solenama Suit land was settled to Dula Mia vide registered patta dated 15-10-1948 and Partly Settlement Khatian No. 151 was recorded for Dula Mia and after SAT Act coming into force, Dula Mia became owner of the Suit land under the Government and RS Khatian (Exhibit-1) was recorded in the name of Dula Mia and he paid rents (Exhibit-3 series). 

 23. CS Khatian [Exhibit-1(Ka)] No.11 shows the record and possession of Sakander Ali and Dula Mia sons of Bande Ali to the extent of 4(four) anna share in the entire land recorded in the khatian. SA Khatian (Exhibit No.1) No. 40 shows the record of right in various plots in the name of Sekander Ali and Dula Mia. 

 This is misreading of evidence. Ext. 1, SA Khatian No. 40, which shows that the names of Sekander Ali and Dula Mia have been recorded in the Khatian. (ii) The finding of the trial court with regard to the possession of the party is not based on consideration of material oral and documentary evidence. The plaintiffs' witnesses in their deposition proved the possession of the plaintiffs. The documentary evidence shows that possession was not taken from the predecessor of the plaintiffs at any point of time by the predecessor of the defendants. 

 (iii) The ownership, possession and also settlement patta of 96 decimals of land in favour of Dula Mia were proved by petty settlement khatian 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the Khatian. 

 (iv) The dismissal of the suit being Title Suit No. 57 of 1988 filed by the defendant-predecessors for recovery of possession of 13 decimals of land of plot o. 361 appertaining khatian No. 40 for the predecessor of the plaintiffs shows that possession remained with plaintiff predecessor. (v) The successors of Abdul Hakim Majumder i.e. the defendants in the present suit filed objection under Rule 30 of the Tenancy rules against record of rights in the name of the plaintiffs and for correcting the record in the name of the defendants. The Revenue Officer by an order dated 06-8-1990 dismissed the objection with the finding as follows: 

 29. The patta executed by Abdul Hakim Majumder (defendants predecessor) in favour of Dula Mia, son of Late Bande Ali (plaintiff's predecessor) shows that about Hakim Majumder executed patta dated 15-10-1948 settling 96 decimals of land in favour of the Dula Mia according to the terms of sole decree in civil Suit No. 19 of 1939. The ownership, and possession and also settlement of Dula Mia in 96 decimals of land are also evidenced from the petty settlement Khatian No. 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the khatian. 

 30. AK Fazlul Haque Majumder, son of late Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Title Suit No. 57 of 1988 against Ayub Ali and others sons of Dula Mia in the court of Assistant Judge, Nangolkot, Comilla for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of 13 decimals of land in plot no. 361 appertaining to khatian No.40 (part of the suit land) which was contested by the defendant in that suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation in the plaint. The plaintiff of that suit did not proceed with the suit as a result the suit was dismissed due to absence of the plaintiff, Ext. Ka/5(Kha) vide order dated 21-9-1991 of the learned Assistant Judge, Nangolkot, Comilla. 

 31. In the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216, in Paragraph-8 it has been held: "Plaintiffs name has also been recorded in SA Khatian and all objections raised by defendant No.1 were overruled by the Revenue office" 

 32. In the present case also the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs were recorded in the CS and SA Khatian and objection filed by the defendant-predecessors against the record in the name of the plaintiff-predecessors was rejected. This shows the possession of the plaintiffs and their predecessor in the suit land.
